text:
Sonnet

You see that

I do not let you go, that I bind myself

to your blond and vaporous memory,

fugitive

in the street and silent,

I, who was power and rapture.

I stretch myself

as far as I can; I doubt and try

to grasp your dress, beautiful because it is yours;

always fitted and at the same time sumptuous,

temptation here and there reserve.

Look at me in

a café in this little square

where traffic crackles and burns in the sun

and where everything, even a streetcar, flies.

I think of

you, of your eyes, of your afternoon...

And I would like to swell like a sail

and I take refuge inside myself, cowardly.

translation.title: I Have Just Passed by the Post Office, Love...
translation.editorial_note: This alternate catalog title preserves the embedded sonnet heading and duplicate source text.
